description: First 50 seeds only - testing 'starting well' quality

scoring_criteria.9: Perfect native speech in both languages
scoring_criteria.1-2: Marginal, no one would say this

phrases.english: And you are learning to find out what the answer is.
phrases.other: E você está aprendendo a descobrir qual é a resposta.
phrases.notes: Both natural. English slightly formal with 'you are' vs 'you're', Portuguese flows well.

phrases.english: I want to go as soon as you can.
phrases.other: Eu quero ir assim que você puder.
phrases.notes: Portuguese excellent with subjunctive 'puder'. English slightly odd - would more naturally say 'as soon as possible' or 'as soon as you can go'.

phrases.english: I'm starting to speak English but I feel a little tired.
phrases.other: Estou começando a falar inglês mas eu me sinto um pouco cansado.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Portuguese reflexive 'me sinto' correct. English contraction good.

phrases.english: I want to speak English
phrases.other: eu quero falar inglês
phrases.notes: Perfect. Simple, natural in both languages.

phrases.english: I was thinking about whether I need to improve this morning.
phrases.other: Eu estava pensando se eu preciso melhorar esta manhã.
phrases.notes: Both understandable but slightly awkward. 'Improve' needs object (improve what?). Portuguese 'se eu preciso' is fine but redundant 'eu'.

phrases.english: I've been learning English and I don't want to interrupt the story.
phrases.other: Estou aprendendo inglês e eu não quero interromper a história.
phrases.notes: Semantically odd pairing but grammatically correct. Portuguese 'Estou aprendendo' for 'I've been learning' loses the duration aspect.

phrases.english: I want to start talking
phrases.other: eu quero começar a falar
phrases.notes: Perfect. Natural in both languages.

phrases.english: he doesn't want to speak
phrases.other: ele não quer falar
phrases.notes: Perfect. Natural contraction in English, correct negation in Portuguese.

phrases.english: he doesn't want to be quiet
phrases.other: ele não quer ficar quieto
phrases.notes: Both natural. Portuguese 'ficar quieto' is the correct idiom.

phrases.english: I know that I need to improve.
phrases.other: Eu sei que eu preciso melhorar.
phrases.notes: Redundant 'eu' in Portuguese (could be 'Sei que preciso'). English 'improve' still lacks object but more acceptable in context.

phrases.english: It's useful to learn as soon as you can.
phrases.other: É útil aprender assim que você puder.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Portuguese subjunctive correct. English flows well.

phrases.english: I started to learn and now I don't want to interrupt you.
phrases.other: Eu comecei a aprender e agora eu não quero interromper você.
phrases.notes: Both grammatically correct. Semantically odd combination. Portuguese could use 'interrompê-lo' for more natural flow.

phrases.english: I want to be able to remember
phrases.other: eu quero conseguir lembrar
phrases.notes: Both natural. 'Conseguir' well chosen for 'be able to'.

phrases.english: I wasn't thinking about how to speak English yesterday.
phrases.other: Eu não estava pensando em como falar inglês ontem.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Portuguese 'pensando em' is correct preposition.

phrases.english: I started to think
phrases.other: eu comecei a pensar
phrases.notes: Perfect. Natural in both languages.

phrases.english: we want to come back
phrases.other: nós queremos voltar
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both completely natural.

phrases.english: I'm not going to be able to remember her name.
phrases.other: Eu não vou conseguir lembrar o nome dela.
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both natural. Portuguese word order excellent.

phrases.english: are you learning English
phrases.other: você está aprendendo inglês
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both natural question forms.

phrases.english: to be able to remember
phrases.other: conseguir lembrar
phrases.notes: Perfect. Infinitive fragments for LEGO building. Both natural.

phrases.english: Do you want to meet at six o'clock later on?
phrases.other: Você quer nos encontrar às seis horas mais tarde?
phrases.notes: Portuguese 'nos encontrar' implies 'meet us' not 'meet' in general - translation mismatch. 'Later on' with specific time is redundant.

phrases.english: You wanted to go and speak more yesterday.
phrases.other: Você queria ir e falar mais ontem.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Simple past in Portuguese correct.

phrases.english: I was feeling tired and I was thinking about whether I want to speak.
phrases.other: Eu estava me sentindo cansado e eu estava pensando se eu quero falar.
phrases.notes: Very repetitive with 'eu estava' twice. English tense shift (was/want) awkward. Functional but clunky.

phrases.english: I'm tired this morning
phrases.other: estou cansado esta manhã
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both natural and idiomatic.

phrases.english: I mean that it's a good thing to learn English as much as possible.
phrases.other: Eu quero dizer que é uma coisa boa aprender inglês o máximo possível.
phrases.notes: Both understandable. 'Uma coisa boa' slightly literal for 'a good thing'. English natural enough.

phrases.english: are you going to help me
phrases.other: você vai me ajudar
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both natural question forms.

phrases.english: I'm trying to speak as often as possible
phrases.other: estou tentando falar o máximo possível
phrases.notes: English natural. Portuguese 'o máximo possível' means 'as much as possible' not 'as often as possible' - slight semantic mismatch.

phrases.english: I'm not trying to finish as quickly as possible.
phrases.other: Eu não estou tentando terminar o mais rápido possível.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Portuguese construction correct.

phrases.english: I'm going to start talking soon
phrases.other: eu vou começar a falar em breve
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both natural. 'Em breve' excellent for 'soon'.

phrases.english: I want to speak English all day
phrases.other: eu quero falar inglês o dia todo
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both natural and idiomatic.

phrases.english: We want to stop talking at six o'clock.
phrases.other: Nós queremos parar de falar às seis horas.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Portuguese 'parar de' correct construction.

phrases.english: I want to learn as often as possible
phrases.other: eu quero aprender o máximo possível
phrases.notes: Same issue as #26: 'o máximo possível' = 'as much as possible', not 'as often as possible'. Semantic mismatch.

phrases.english: what the answer is
phrases.other: qual é a resposta
phrases.notes: Perfect. Fragment for embedded clause. Both natural.

phrases.english: I'm not sure if I can guess what's going to happen today
phrases.other: não tenho certeza se eu consigo adivinhar o que vai acontecer hoje
phrases.notes: Both natural. Portuguese slightly long but grammatically correct.

phrases.english: I'm not trying to learn
phrases.other: eu não estou tentando aprender
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both natural.

phrases.english: she wants to find out what the answer is
phrases.other: ela quer descobrir qual é a resposta
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both natural.

phrases.english: before I have to go
phrases.other: antes de eu ter que ir
phrases.notes: Both natural. Portuguese personal infinitive correct.

phrases.english: He started to learn English last month and he wants to speak now.
phrases.other: Ele comeceu a aprender inglês no mês passado e ele quer falar agora.
phrases.notes: CRITICAL ERROR: Portuguese has 'comeceu' which is WRONG - should be 'começou'. This is a conjugation error (preterite of começar).

phrases.english: how long have you been speaking
phrases.other: há quanto tempo você está falando
phrases.notes: Perfect. Portuguese 'há quanto tempo + present' is the correct idiom for English present perfect continuous.

phrases.english: How long have you been feeling nearly ready?
phrases.other: Há quanto tempo você está sentindo quase pronto?
phrases.notes: Portuguese awkward - 'sentindo quase pronto' doesn't work. Should be 'se sentindo quase pronto' (reflexive) or restructured. English is slightly unusual but acceptable.

phrases.english: You wanted to speak English with her.
phrases.other: Você queria falar inglês com ela.
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both natural.

phrases.english: I'm not trying to finish because I feel a little tired.
phrases.other: Eu não estou tentando terminar porque eu me sinto um pouco cansado.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Portuguese reflexive correct.

phrases.english: do you speak English
phrases.other: você fala inglês?
phrases.notes: Perfect. Classic phrase, both natural.

phrases.english: We don't want to learn English with you this afternoon.
phrases.other: Nós não queremos aprender inglês com você esta tarde.
phrases.notes: Both grammatically correct and natural, though context is unusual (why would you tell someone this?).

phrases.english: But I don't want to learn her name later on.
phrases.other: Mas eu não quero aprender o nome dela mais tarde.
phrases.notes: Semantically odd - 'learn someone's name' is unusual phrasing in both languages. 'Find out' or 'saber' would be more natural.

phrases.english: I want to ask you before you go.
phrases.other: Eu quero te perguntar antes de você ir.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Portuguese personal infinitive correct.

phrases.english: I started this morning
phrases.other: eu comecei esta manhã
phrases.notes: Perfect. Both natural.

phrases.english: You wanted to interrupt and I wanted to speak with you.
phrases.other: Você queria interromper e eu queria falar com você.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Good parallel structure.

phrases.english: Did you want to think about it carefully last month?
phrases.other: Você queria pensar nisso com cuidado no mês passado?
phrases.notes: Perfect. 'Nisso' is the correct contraction (em+isso). Both natural.

phrases.english: She doesn't want to think about it and she wants to speak English with you.
phrases.other: Ela não quer pensar nisso e ela quer falar inglês com você.
phrases.notes: Both natural. 'Nisso' correct. Slightly repetitive 'ela' but acceptable.

phrases.english: She wants to meet and find out the answer.
phrases.other: Ela quer nos encontrar e descobrir a resposta.
phrases.notes: Portuguese 'nos encontrar' = 'meet us', but English says just 'meet' - semantic mismatch. Same issue as #20.

phrases_below_5.english: He started to learn English last month and he wants to speak now.
phrases_below_5.other: Ele comeceu a aprender inglês no mês passado e ele quer falar agora.
phrases_below_5.reason: CRITICAL: Portuguese conjugation error - 'comeceu' should be 'começou'. This is a fundamental verb conjugation mistake.

phrases_below_5.english: How long have you been feeling nearly ready?
phrases_below_5.other: Há quanto tempo você está sentindo quase pronto?
phrases_below_5.reason: Missing reflexive - Portuguese should be 'se sentindo' for 'feeling'. The phrase is awkward and ungrammatical.

worst_3_phrases.english: He started to learn English last month and he wants to speak now.
worst_3_phrases.other: Ele comeceu a aprender inglês no mês passado e ele quer falar agora.
worst_3_phrases.reason: CRITICAL CONJUGATION ERROR: 'comeceu' is incorrect. The preterite of 'começar' is 'começou'. This is a significant error that would confuse learners and teach wrong Portuguese.

worst_3_phrases.english: How long have you been feeling nearly ready?
worst_3_phrases.other: Há quanto tempo você está sentindo quase pronto?
worst_3_phrases.reason: MISSING REFLEXIVE: 'sentir-se' (to feel) requires reflexive pronoun. Should be 'você está SE sentindo quase pronto'. Also 'quase pronto' placement is awkward.

worst_3_phrases.english: I was feeling tired and I was thinking about whether I want to speak.
worst_3_phrases.other: Eu estava me sentindo cansado e eu estava pensando se eu quero falar.
worst_3_phrases.reason: OVERLY REPETITIVE: Four uses of 'eu' in Portuguese makes it sound non-native. Also tense inconsistency (was thinking... want) in English is awkward.

summary.quality_assessment: GOOD - Round 3 shows strong overall quality with an average of 7.88/9. The vast majority of phrases (43/50) score 7 or higher. However, one critical conjugation error (idx 37: 'comeceu' instead of 'começou') needs immediate correction. Two additional phrases have structural issues requiring attention. The 'meet/encontrar' translation shows a recurring issue where 'nos encontrar' (meet us) is used for simple 'meet' - worth reviewing for consistency.
key_issues_identified: CRITICAL: Verb conjugation error in phrase 37 - 'comeceu' must be 'começou'
Missing reflexive pronoun in phrase 39 - 'sentindo' needs 'se sentindo'
Semantic mismatch in phrases 20 and 50 - 'nos encontrar' vs 'meet'
Phrases 26 and 31 - 'o máximo possível' means 'as much as possible' not 'as often as possible'
Occasional redundant pronouns in Portuguese (multiple 'eu' in same sentence)
